\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شرشف} (sharshaf)}{شرشف (sharshaf)}]{\ar{شرشف} (sharshaf) — a bedsheet}

\label{lesson:AR-C551-sharshaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to polish, then the Arabic for to maintain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شرشف}}
\textbf{\ar{شرشف}} — \emph{sharshaf} — \textquotedblleft{}a bedsheet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{غيرت} \ar{أمي} \ar{شراشف} \ar{السرير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghayyarat ummī sharāshif as-sarīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother changed the bedsheets.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{شراشف}, \emph{sharāshif}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شرشف}} (\emph{sharshaf}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{chādar-shab}, \textquotedblleft{}a night sheet\textquotedblright{}, which reached Arabic through Turkish.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharshaf}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharshaf}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghayyarat ummī sharāshif as-sarīr.} — My mother changed the bedsheets.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to polish, then the Arabic for to maintain, then say \emph{sharshaf} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شرشف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bedsheet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مخدة} (mikhadda)}{مخدة (mikhadda)}]{\ar{مخدة} (mikhadda) — a cushion; a pillow}

\label{lesson:AR-C551-mikhadda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to maintain, then the Arabic for a bedsheet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مخدة}}
\textbf{\ar{مخدة}} — \emph{mikhadda} — \textquotedblleft{}a cushion; a pillow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وضعت} \ar{المخدة} \ar{تحت} \ar{رأسي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waḍaʿtu al-mikhadda taḥta raʾsī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I put the cushion under my head.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مخدة}} (\emph{mikhadda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to furrow; the cheek\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives mikhadda as a pillow, so called because it is put under the cheek, khadd, which you know.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mikhadda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mikhadda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waḍaʿtu al-mikhadda taḥta raʾsī.} — I put the cushion under my head.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to maintain, then the Arabic for a bedsheet, then say \emph{mikhadda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مخدة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cushion; a pillow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حوض} (ḥawḍ)}{حوض (ḥawḍ)}]{\ar{حوض} (ḥawḍ) — a basin, a tub}

\label{lesson:AR-C551-hawd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a bedsheet, then the Arabic for a cushion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حوض}}
\textbf{\ar{حوض}} — \emph{ḥawḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}a basin, a tub\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ملأ} \ar{الولد} \ar{حوض} \ar{الاستحمام} \ar{بالماء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{malaʾa al-walad ḥawḍ al-istiḥmām bi-l-māʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boy filled the bathtub with water.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أحواض}, \emph{aḥwāḍ}.

\ar{حوض} \ar{الاستحمام} is a bathtub.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حوض}} (\emph{ḥawḍ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-w-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}a watering trough\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives ḥawḍ as a trough or cistern for water.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥawḍ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥawḍ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malaʾa al-walad ḥawḍ al-istiḥmām bi-l-māʾ.} — The boy filled the bathtub with water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a bedsheet, then the Arabic for a cushion, then say \emph{ḥawḍ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حوض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A basin, a tub\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ممسحة} (mimsaḥa)}{ممسحة (mimsaḥa)}]{\ar{ممسحة} (mimsaḥa) — a mop}

\label{lesson:AR-C551-mimsaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a cushion, then the Arabic for a basin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ممسحة}}
\textbf{\ar{ممسحة}} — \emph{mimsaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}a mop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نظفت} \ar{الأرض} \ar{بالممسحة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naẓẓaftu al-arḍ bi-l-mimsaḥa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I cleaned the floor with the mop.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ممسحة}} (\emph{mimsaḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-s-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to wipe\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Masaḥa, to wipe, which you know, is from the same root; the pattern mifʿala names a tool.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mimsaḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mimsaḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naẓẓaftu al-arḍ bi-l-mimsaḥa.} — I cleaned the floor with the mop.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a cushion, then the Arabic for a basin, then say \emph{mimsaḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كنبة} (kanaba)}{كنبة (kanaba)}]{\ar{كنبة} (kanaba) — a couch}

\label{lesson:AR-C551-kanaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a basin, then the Arabic for a mop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كنبة}}
\textbf{\ar{كنبة}} — \emph{kanaba} — \textquotedblleft{}a couch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{جلسنا} \ar{على} \ar{الكنبة} \ar{وشاهدنا} \ar{فيلما}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jalasnā ʿalā al-kanaba wa-shāhadnā fīlman.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We sat on the couch and watched a film.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كنبة}} (\emph{kanaba}) is a modern word, usually traced to French \emph{canapé}, a sofa.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kanaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kanaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalasnā ʿalā al-kanaba wa-shāhadnā fīlman.} — We sat on the couch and watched a film.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a basin, then the Arabic for a mop, then say \emph{kanaba} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 544–551 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R551-review-544-551}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for an oud and a violin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an oud, a violin, a drum, a reed flute, a band
  \item a poet, a rhyme, to recite, to create, to direct films
  \item a half, a supporter, to finish level, to pass the ball, to compete
  \item a triumph, a championship, a trophy, a medal, to qualify
  \item swimming, boxing, to wrestle, to compete with, to punch
  \item an attic, a bell, a handle, a bolt, a drain
  \item a chandelier, a vase, to shake out, to polish, to maintain
  \item a bedsheet, a cushion, a basin, a mop, a couch
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An oud? (\textbf{\ar{عود}}, \emph{ʿūd}.) A violin? (\textbf{\ar{كمان}}, \emph{kamān}.) A drum? (\textbf{\ar{طبل}}, \emph{ṭabl}.) A reed flute? (\textbf{\ar{ناي}}, \emph{nāy}.) A band? (\textbf{\ar{فرقة}}, \emph{firqa}.) A poet? (\textbf{\ar{شاعر}}, \emph{shāʿir}.) A rhyme? (\textbf{\ar{قافية}}, \emph{qāfiya}.) To recite? (\textbf{\ar{أنشد}}, \emph{anshada}.) To create? (\textbf{\ar{أبدع}}, \emph{abdaʿa}.) To direct films? (\textbf{\ar{أخرج}}, \emph{akhraja}.) A half? (\textbf{\ar{شوط}}, \emph{shawṭ}.) A supporter? (\textbf{\ar{مشجع}}, \emph{mushajjiʿ}.) To finish level? (\textbf{\ar{تعادل}}, \emph{taʿādala}.) To pass the ball? (\textbf{\ar{مرر}}, \emph{marrara}.) To compete? (\textbf{\ar{تنافس}}, \emph{tanāfasa}.) A triumph? (\textbf{\ar{فوز}}, \emph{fawz}.) A championship? (\textbf{\ar{بطولة}}, \emph{buṭūla}.) A trophy? (\textbf{\ar{كأس}}, \emph{kaʾs}.) A medal? (\textbf{\ar{ميدالية}}, \emph{mīdāliya}.) To qualify? (\textbf{\ar{تأهل}}, \emph{taʾahhala}.) Swimming? (\textbf{\ar{سباحة}}, \emph{sibāḥa}.) Boxing? (\textbf{\ar{ملاكمة}}, \emph{mulākama}.) To wrestle? (\textbf{\ar{صارع}}, \emph{ṣāraʿa}.) To compete with? (\textbf{\ar{نافس}}, \emph{nāfasa}.) To punch? (\textbf{\ar{لكم}}, \emph{lakama}.) An attic? (\textbf{\ar{علية}}, \emph{ʿulliyya}.) A bell? (\textbf{\ar{جرس}}, \emph{jaras}.) A handle? (\textbf{\ar{مقبض}}, \emph{miqbaḍ}.) A bolt? (\textbf{\ar{مزلاج}}, \emph{mizlāj}.) A drain? (\textbf{\ar{بالوعة}}, \emph{bālūʿa}.) A chandelier? (\textbf{\ar{ثريا}}, \emph{thurayyā}.) A vase? (\textbf{\ar{مزهرية}}, \emph{mazhariyya}.) To shake out? (\textbf{\ar{نفض}}, \emph{nafaḍa}.) To polish? (\textbf{\ar{لمع}}, \emph{lammaʿa}.) To maintain? (\textbf{\ar{صان}}, \emph{ṣāna}.) A bedsheet? (\textbf{\ar{شرشف}}, \emph{sharshaf}.) A cushion? (\textbf{\ar{مخدة}}, \emph{mikhadda}.) A basin? (\textbf{\ar{حوض}}, \emph{ḥawḍ}.) A mop? (\textbf{\ar{ممسحة}}, \emph{mimsaḥa}.) A couch? (\textbf{\ar{كنبة}}, \emph{kanaba}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
